verified.catalyst: The STB's final decision on Union Pacific's acquisition of NSC for 1 UNP share plus $88.82 cash per NSC share. Approval would collapse the spread to UNP + $88.82.
verified.dated_milestone: 2026-09-22: STB rejected the motions to dismiss the revised application (per triage; not re-verified this run). Next: STB evidentiary and comment deadlines, then a final decision expected in early 2027. The exact date is unconfirmed because no web lookup was possible.
verified.instrument: Long NSC / short 1.0x UNP per NSC share (hedged arb). An unhedged long NSC is mostly a UNP beta bet.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: the counterparty is Union Pacific. G2 yes: a signed merger agreement with fixed terms of 1 UNP + $88.82 cash. G3 partial: the gross spread is about $48.9 (14.1%), which the market is pricing as STB regulatory risk rather than leaving unpriced.
verified.edge: M/L. The deal value is contractual, so it is exempt from the numerator-provenance rule: 306.49 + 88.82 = $395.31 against NSC at $346.45, a 14.1% gross spread (2026-11-02 FMP). (a) Run-up: NSC was roughly $255-260 before the July 2025 talks leaked (from memory, not re-verified), so it is up about 33-35%. Part of that is UNP's own rally (UNP 52-week range $216-316). (b) Remaining: 14.1% gross to approval, against about 19% downside to a standalone floor of roughly $280 (NSC 52-week low $277.8). That implies about a 57% market-implied approval probability. This is less harvested than the triage label "late-arc" suggests, but the spread is wide because regulatory risk is real: this is the first Class I mega-merger under the 2001 STB rules, with active opposition. The edge is only as good as our read on STB approval odds, and we have no differentiated view on that.

verified.catalyst: Topline from PREDICT-1, the registrational symptom trial of topical licaminlimab (anti-TNFR1) in genotype-enriched dry eye disease, guided for around year-end 2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Randomization completed 2026-10-19 (176 patients, 2/3 carry the TNFR1 high-responder variant). Topline guided 'around year-end' 2026 (PR 2026-10-07), so expect late Dec 2026 to Jan 2027. Q3 results are the next checkpoint, likely mid-Nov 2026.
verified.instrument: OCS common (Nasdaq; also XICE). Close to the readout, defined-risk calls or call spreads are an option, but options liquidity was not checked.
verified.bloom_gates: G2 only: the company has made a concrete, dated commitment to a registrational topline around year-end, repeated in the 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-19 PRs. G1 fails because there is no named counterparty, partner or acquirer. G3 is weak: no specific unpriced figure is contractual, and the upside comes from a probability-weighted readout.
verified.edge: M-L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about +8% (7.32 close on randomization day 2026-10-19 to 7.92 on 2026-11-02). Measured from the 2026-10-07 guidance PR (8.50) the stock is -7%, and it is down about -77% from the 52-week high of 34.48, so this readout is not harvested. Remaining capture: about +45% to roughly $11.5 on a clean positive result, against about -35 to -40% to roughly $5 on a miss. The $5 floor is cash of about $3.8/share plus residual value for privosegtor (optic neuritis). The capital structure is clean: no preferred, debt of only CHF 2.5M in leases, CHF 233M of current assets at 6/30/26, and market cap about $485M. Probability-weighted at about 40% success for a dry-eye symptom endpoint, expected value is close to today's price. The edge comes from the unpriced, dated binary and the cash floor, not from mispricing.
verified.primary_source: Oculis PR 'Oculis Completes Randomization in PREDICT-1 Registrational Trial of Licaminlimab for TNFR1-Mediated Dry Eye Disease' (GlobeNewswire, 2026-10-19); Oculis PR re Eyecelerator @ AAO, 'PREDICT-1 ... on track for topline readout around year-end' (GlobeNewswire, 2026-10-07); FMP quote and EOD history (2026-11-02); FMP Q2-2026 balance sheet (filed 2026-08-06).
verified.analysis: The catalyst is real, specific, dated and forward. Randomization is complete and the company guided topline around year-end, so this is a true unfired binary, and the stock shows no run-up: it has fallen from about 14.5 in June to 7.9 and is flat-to-up only 8% since randomization. The risks are dry-eye trials' history of failure on symptom endpoints, the small n=176 study, and a pipeline narrative that has moved toward privosegtor in neuro-ophthalmology, which cushions a miss but dilutes the upside. The waterfall is clean (no prefs, cash covers about half the market cap), so the score is on the event. It stays WATCH rather than ACTIVE because at about 40% odds the expected value is roughly symmetric. GAP: web search budget was exhausted, so I could not verify the PREDICT-1 primary endpoint, the Phase 2 effect size in variant carriers, whether a second registrational trial is needed, or Q3 cash and runway. FMP press releases were the only source.
